extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers planning or conducting systematic reviews/evidence syntheses (e.g., nursing, social work, health and social science researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on whether, where, and how to register a protocol for a systematic review or other evidence synthesis, including discipline-appropriate registries, registry-specific requirements, and what to include in a protocol. Aimed at researchers preparing a protocol prior to conducting a review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register your protocol before beginning research
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on your discipline and needs for your review, consider registering your protocol before beginning your research. Registering your protocol promotes transparency and helps avoid questionable research practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registering at inception is recommended to increase transparency and reduce questionable research practices; treat registration as an early step in planning your review rather than an afterthought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PROSPERO for reviews with a health-related outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: PROSPERO is an international database of prospectively registered systematic reviews with a health-related outcome. PROSPERO aims to provide a comprehensive listing of systematic reviews registered at inception to help avoid duplication and reduce opportunity for reporting bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check PROSPERO's Guidance Notes and Inclusion Criteria before submitting. Submitting a protocol to PROSPERO does not prevent you from publishing in the journal of your choice. Use 'Search PROSPERO' to discover previously registered work and avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use OSF Registries for discipline-agnostic preregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: OSF Registries (Center for Open Science) is a free, open platform for registering projects in any discipline. Upon registration a time-stamped version of the project is created that cannot be edited or deleted and is intended to act as a preserved version of a project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using OSF, write out specific details such as data collection methods, analysis plans, and rules for data exclusion so important decisions are documented early. Search OSF Registries to discover previously registered work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow organizational templates and guidance (Cochrane, JBI, Campbell)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations such as the Cochrane Collaboration, Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI), or Campbell Collaboration have their own guidance and templates for systematic reviews — contact the organizations for additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the organization's handbook or template (e.g., Cochrane Handbook, JBI Manual) when preparing protocols for reviews intended to follow that organization's methods; these templates often specify required protocol elements and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochrane protocols: strict methodological standards and publication commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane publishes protocols that meet their strict guidelines. If a review protocol is accepted, you must publish your review as a Cochrane Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search the Cochrane Library and 'Our Evidence' to ensure your proposal does not duplicate existing Cochrane-registered or commenced reviews. Consult Chapter II: Planning a Cochrane Review and the Cochrane MECIR manual for detailed requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to MECIR standards for Cochrane reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The MECIR Standards are methodological expectations of Cochrane Intervention Reviews for the conduct and reporting of new Cochrane intervention reviews, reporting of protocols, and updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat MECIR as required methodological standards for Cochrane protocols and reviews; consult the MECIR documentation when drafting protocol methods and reporting plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campbell Collaboration: social science reviews and publication expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Campbell is an international social science research network producing high quality, policy-relevant evidence syntheses. If you submit your protocol to Campbell you are committing to publish your review in Campbell Systematic Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search Campbell Title Registrations to find accepted titles and avoid duplication. Follow Campbell Systematic Reviews' policies and the Methodological Expectations of Campbell Collaboration Intervention Reviews (MECCIR) provided in Campbell Author Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to MECCIR standards for Campbell reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: MECCIR sets methodological expectations for the conduct and reporting of Campbell intervention reviews (analogous to Cochrane's MECIR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download and follow MECCIR conduct and reporting standards from the Campbell Author Guidelines when preparing protocols intended for Campbell.

rubrics_metrics.name: JBI Systematic Review Register: affiliation-limited registration to promote collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: The JBI Systematic Review Register is for use by JBI-affiliated entities only. Registration of a systematic review title on the JBI website is to promote collaboration between affiliated entities and to recognize that the registered topic is currently in development to avoid unintended duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are JBI-affiliated, register to make others aware of ongoing work. Consult the JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis (e.g., section 3.2 on protocol development for effectiveness evidence) for detailed protocol development guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search registries before registering to avoid duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Use registry search functions (PROSPERO, OSF Registries, Cochrane Library, Campbell Title Registrations) to discover previously registered work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform searches across relevant registries as part of planning to ensure your review question is not already being addressed; registry searches are a practical step to reduce unnecessary duplication of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include detailed protocol elements (methods, analysis, exclusion rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write out specific details such as data collection methods, analysis plans, and rules for data exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing explicit methods and decision rules in the protocol documents important a priori choices, enhances transparency, and allows the time-stamped registry entry to serve as a preserved record of those choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of registry-specific obligations and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Different registries have different eligibility criteria, scope, and obligations (e.g., PROSPERO is for health-related outcomes; Cochrane and Campbell may require publication in their journals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before selecting a registry, review its inclusion/eligibility criteria and any commitments (e.g., mandatory publication venues); choose the registry appropriate to your discipline, topic, and intended publication pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use handbooks and manuals for methodological detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Handbooks and manuals (e.g., Cochrane Handbook; JBI manual; Searching for Studies: A Guide to Information Retrieval for Campbell reviews) provide comprehensive methodological guidance for planning and writing protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these resources for detailed instructions on protocol structure, search methods, study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment relevant to your review type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the archival nature of registries (prospective, time-stamped records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations (e.g., OSF time-stamped registries, PROSPERO's prospective registration) create preserved records of the protocol at inception that are not editable in ways that erase the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use registries to create an immutable record of your planned methods and decisions; this supports transparency and helps detect post hoc changes to methods that could introduce bias.
